outcome: Help authorised users find, compare, and reuse trusted institutional and research knowledge with citations.
overview: Institutional knowledge sits in repositories, shared drives, journal subscriptions and individual teams, so researchers and policy staff spend hours locating sources they are entitled to see and sometimes repeat work already done. This solution indexes permissioned repositories, answers questions only from sources the signed-in user may already access, and shows the citation, publication date and licence behind every passage. Research workspaces let users compare evidence, flag contradictions and export a review brief that states its own limitations. A six-to-ten-week pilot on one repository tests permission fidelity, retrieval relevance and citation completeness before any wider rollout; the tool never asserts research correctness, and reviewing the cited sources stays the researcher’s job.

benefits.text: Reduce the time to find and validate an approved source set for selected research tasks by a target 40%
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue; to validate against a measured search-time baseline
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate on a defined task set in the pilot — not a guarantee across all research work

benefits.text: Show a citation, publication date and licence for every passage returned, so evidence can be checked rather than trusted
benefits.source: Reference design — citation enforcement and rights metadata are structural to the retrieval layer
benefits.limits: Depends on repository metadata quality; sources with no reliable date or rights record are excluded from the index

benefits.text: Reduce duplicated studies and repeated internal requests by making existing institutional work discoverable to those entitled to see it
benefits.source: Redington Education catalogue — validated capacity and avoided duplication
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Duplication avoidance is hard to attribute; the pilot measures proxies such as repeat requests and reused collections

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (UAE, KSA); indexed content, embeddings and query logs stay inside the institution’s tenancy, and a private enclave option keeps confidential research isolated

notFor.situation: Repositories have no owner, no access model and no usable metadata
notFor.why: Identity-aware retrieval depends on knowing who may see what; without an access model the index either over-shares or is useless

notFor.situation: The institution expects the system to judge whether research findings are correct
notFor.why: The design retrieves and cites; it does not adjudicate scientific validity, and researcher review of cited sources remains mandatory by policy

notFor.situation: Publisher licences do not permit indexing or machine processing of subscribed content
notFor.why: Indexing licensed material outside its terms exposes the institution to rights claims and can end the subscription

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the institution owns repository rights, classification decisions and research-integrity policy · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; 12–24 weeks to scaled federated deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, search and retrieval engineer, integration engineer, information-security specialist; customer research office lead, librarian, identity owner, content stewards · Support model: Business-hours support aligned to research and academic calendars; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation and a defined path for permission incidents
1) Discovery, repository inventory and rights map
2) Classification review and index design
3) Connector and retrieval build
4) Gold-question evaluation and permission testing
5) Security, red-team and export-control testing
6) Pilot, time study and handover
deliverables: Permission tests pass with no user retrieving content they could not open at source
Retrieval relevance meets the agreed threshold on the gold-question set
Citation, date and licence present on every returned passage
Safe refusal demonstrated where evidence is thin or out of scope
Export controls enforced in line with the rights map
Security testing passed and researcher and library UAT completed
effort: 6–10 weeks pilot; 12–24 weeks to scaled federated deployment
languages: English delivery; Arabic and English content indexing and answering supported
